html:
Betty's Hope was a sugar plantation on Antigua, run by the Codrington family from 1674 for nearly three centuries. It was among the first large sugar estates on the island.

Christopher Codrington came from Barbados and brought its system of sugar grown and boiled by enslaved Africans. Antigua soon became almost one big plantation, with windmills on every rise. The family also leased the island of Barbuda, using it to raise food and stock for the estates.

After emancipation the estate went on with paid labour until the 1940s. A restored windmill and museum on the site now tell the story of the enslaved people who worked it.
